bull.b: Zscaler’s subscription-led model has produced substantial multi-year revenue expansion, supported by recurring customer contracts and broader platform adoption. This creates a durable base for upselling users, products and modules while increasing the company’s ability to invest in growth and operating leverage.

Consistently positive free cash flow provides financial flexibility despite reported accounting losses. Strong cash conversion can fund product development, infrastructure and go-to-market investment internally, while reducing reliance on external financing as the platform continues to scale.

Expansion across Zero Trust, AI security and related platform capabilities broadens Zscaler’s addressable opportunity beyond its original core products. Rising enterprise adoption and new workloads can support cross-selling, larger contracts and a more diversified recurring-revenue base over time.

bear.b: Persistent GAAP operating and net losses show that the business has not yet converted its strong gross margins and recurring revenue into durable bottom-line profitability. Continued investment and non-cash expenses may delay earnings maturation and leave execution sensitive to growth or cost pressures.

Management expects growth to slow materially from fiscal 2026 while infrastructure investment remains elevated. Higher CapEx and lower anticipated growth can limit near-term operating leverage, reduce cash conversion, and increase the execution burden required to sustain attractive long-term returns.

Elevated churn in the acquired MDR business can pressure retention, recurring revenue quality and integration economics. Continued higher renewal losses may require additional selling effort to replace attrition and could make the broader platform’s growth less efficient while the offering is integrated.
